# fethr

> fethr is a featherweight code editor with first-class AI agent integration,
> currently under construction. The name is pronounced "feather".

## What it is

- A minimal, fast desktop code editor where an AI coding agent is a first-class
  peer process, not a bolted-on extension: the editor forwards context
  (selection, files, project) and renders results (streams, diffs); the
  intelligence lives in the agent runtime.
- Designed around the front-end/runtime split popularized by Claude Code.
  fethr is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic.
- No extension platform by design: language intelligence via LSP, syntax via
  tree-sitter, agent via its own protocol.

## Status

Alpha. `npx @evojewel/fethr@alpha .` opens a working editor with an agent panel: a local
server bound to 127.0.0.1 with the OS browser as the shell, CodeMirror 6 core, file tree,
syntax highlighting (JS/TS, Python, Markdown, HTML, CSS, JSON), edit and save. No Electron.
File access is confined to the launch directory.

The agent panel (Cmd-J) runs on the Claude Agent SDK using the machine's existing Claude
Code login. It is read-only by construction (Read/Grep/Glob only; all mutating tools
disabled); its sole change mechanism is a propose_edit tool whose proposals render as diff
cards the writer accepts or rejects — accepted edits apply in the editor, never directly
to disk.
